messages.subject: Multiple Group CFA Modeling
parts:
I have been working on a CFA where model fit is assessed for the sample as a whole, and also with genders separately. When I run the model on the whole group, we get single error variances for each factor as we would expect. However, if we run the model with genders separately OR with the Satorra-Bentler scaled chi-square, we get grouped error variances on all factors. More specifically, there is a triangle error term with triple headed arrows. Furthermore, the grouped error variances don't seem to correspond to anything in the data (i.e., I don't have anything with three groups that would lend itself to the error variances). Unfortunately, it will not let me upload the path diagrams into this message. Is this just a weird graphical thing that does not actually impact my model (I do not think that my degrees of freedom have been changing)? Here are the fitmeasures codes I have been using:

Running model on the whole sample:
fitfullgrouped = cfa(model1, data = imputeddata, orthogonal = FALSE)
summary(fitfullgrouped)
fitmeasures(fitfullgrouped)
semPaths(fitfullgrouped)

Separating groups:
fitfullgrouped = cfa(model1, data = imputeddata, orthogonal = FALSE, group="genderString")
summary(fitfullgrouped)
fitmeasures(fitfullgrouped)
semPaths(fitfullgrouped)

Using Satorra-Bentler scaled chi-square:
fitfullgrouped = cfa(model1, data = imputeddata, orthogonal = FALSE, test="satorra.bentler")
summary(fitfullgrouped)
fitmeasures(fitfullgrouped)
semPaths(fitfullgrouped)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multiple Group CFA Modeling
parts:
You do not get any triple-headed arrows.  Those are just the  same double-headed arrows for the error variances, but there is also a single-headed arrow pointing from the triangle representing the mean structure.  The reason you see those only for the multigroup models is simply a result of lavaan's default settings.  The cfa() function will set meanstructure = FALSE unless any of the following circumstances occur: setting missing = "FIML", there are multiple groups, you use a robust correction that requires mean structure to be estimated, or there are categorical outcomes (requiring a threshold model).  If you want to see consistent graphs, you can simply add the argument meanstructure = TRUE to the single-group cfa() call.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
